suggested_experiment_name: Irreducible axion background (freeze-in X-ray + CMB recast)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 1
notes: Paper derives new cosmological constraints on axions from an irreducible freeze-in abundance (TRH = 5 MeV) recast through DM-decay searches (X-ray, CRB, CMB, spectral distortions). Full exclusion curves span 100 eV - 100 MeV (Figs. 1-2) but numerical curves are only in figures/public data release; the only explicit numerical values in text are g_agamma < 8.1e-14 GeV^-1 at ma = 10 keV (photophilic case, extracted here) and g_aee < 8.0e-15 at 100 keV (photophobic case, a separate AxionElectron limit not encoded here since only one coupling_type is allowed). The bound is strongly mass-dependent, so only the single explicit text value is emitted rather than inventing a flat line. No local DM density assumption applies (cosmological, not haloscope). Confidence level not explicitly stated in extracted text; underlying DM decay limits are typically 95%. Full data available at github.com/nickrodd/IrreducibleAxionAbundance. | [VISION GATE D] vision notes admit tracing a compilation envelope ('envelope of the paper's NEW irreducible-background constraints') rather than the paper's own single curve | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0.65, 35)) | Vision: Fig. 1 (page 2) shows constraints on the photophilic axion (g_aee=0) for T_RH = 5 MeV: g_agamma [GeV^-1] vs m_a [keV], x from 1e-2 to ~4e5 keV (i.e. 10 eV to 4e8 eV), y from ~3e-17 to 3e-9 GeV^-1. Traced the lower envelope of the paper's NEW irreducible-background constraints: the mustard X-ray region (dominant from ~0.5 keV to ~2 MeV, jagged boundary; anchored at the abstract's quoted value g_agamma = 8.1e-14 GeV^-1 at m_a = 10 keV, approximate slope g ~ m^-1.15) and the velvet CMB-anisotropy region (2-30 MeV, minimum ~5e-16 GeV^-1 near 20-25 MeV, then steep rise at the 2m_e / high-mass edge). Light-gray regions (HB stars, SN1987A, Solar Basin) are prior constraints and were excluded from the trace. Fig. 2 (page 3, fig_02) is the photophobic analogue with g_aee, not traced. Boundary jaggedness in the X-ray region introduces up to factor ~2 uncertainty in coupling values; masses converted from keV to eV (x1e3). Axions are assumed NOT to be the dark matter (irreducible freeze-in fraction), so no DM density is assumed. | Calibration: No calibration needed (spot-check verify/stage2 raw_ratio=1.59 snapped to identity)
